summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Krishnath College, served at the National Archives, was founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and held a professorship at Calcutta.
Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and Richard Gombrich, earning a DPhil from the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) by 2003, and was a lecturer and research fellow at Stanford University (attested 2005).

Noboru Karashima specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts there from assistant to professor emeritus, taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and served as president of several international academic associations.

Noboru Miyata worked in religious studies, Japanology, and folklore history. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he held faculty posts at Tokyo Gakugei University, the University of Tsukuba, and Kanagawa University.
Noboru Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and Mejiro University, where he was a professor (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe, Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Ichijo Ogawa, later serving as professor at Otani University and president of its junior college.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He held assistant professorships at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo and served on the faculty at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, advancing from assistant to professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University from around 1951 to 1959 and later served there as an assistant professor from around 1968 to 1975.

Tensho Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a doctorate from the University of Tokyo, he held research positions at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo, and taught as a part-time lecturer at Tokyo University of Agriculture.

Nobumi Iyanaga works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, lectured at the University of Tokyo, held a research contract with the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, and served as representative director of the Société Franco-Japonaise des Études Orientales.

Nobumichi Kusumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who received a PhD from Hiroshima University in 2001 under Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University and served there as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Osaka, Otani, and Yale Universities under scholars including Stanley Weinstein and Noritoshi Aramaki, he held posts at several junior colleges before becoming a professor at Waseda University in 2015.

Nobuyuki Kaji is a philosopher and Sinologist. After studying at Kyoto and Tohoku Universities, he taught at Koyasan, Nagoya, and Osaka Universities, served as president of Koshien Junior College, and later held appointments at Doshisha and Ritsumeikan Universities.

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University and later as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University from 2007 to 2011.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki, held teaching and research roles at Otani University, and served as director of the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute.
